q: Lecture 6 – Eyelids – slide 4: what does this picture show? Describe it.
a:
Viral infection

  • Herpes Simplex of the Eyelids
  • Etiology:
  • when latent herpes simplex viruses present in the tissue are activated by ultraviolet radiation.
  • Signs
  • eritematous eruption in the area of the ophthalmic nerve (V)
  • adenopathy of the local lymph nodes
  • vesicles (after a couple days)
  • clear liquid which becomes turbid
  • eventually covered with crusts
  • crusts fall leaving a pigmented skin with anesthesia or hyperesthesia

q: Lecture 6 – Eyelids – slide 7: what does this picture show? Describe it.
a:
Viral infection

  • Varicella zoster virus
  • Symptoms:
  • severe pain in the area of the first branch of the trigeminal nerve
  • erythema, swelling, photosensitivity, lacrimation
  • clear watery vesicles
  • The vesicles burst and brownish scabs form
  • Blepharitis in 50–70% of all cases.
  • usually immunocompromised persons

q: Lecture 6 – Eyelids – slide 17: what does this picture show? Describe it.
a:
External sty

  • acute sepsis inflammation
  • staphylococcus
  • sebaceous gland (Zeis’s gland) associated with eyelash root.
  • Signs
  • circumscribed inflammatory swelling at free eyelid margin and neighbouring eyelid tissue
  • yellow point with elimination of pus
  • Treatment
  • hot compresses for collection of the pus,
  • pulling out the infected eyelash
  • antiobiotic drops topically.

q: Lecture 6 – Eyelids – slide 24: what does this picture show? Describe it.
a:
Entropion

  • Spastic entropion
  • usually at the lower eyelid in elderly patients and children
  • chronic blepharo-conjunctivitis
  • prolonged ocular patching.
  • The structures supporting the lower eyelid (palpebral ligaments, tarsus, and eyelid retractor) may become lax with age, causing the tarsus to tilt inward.
  • the fibers of the orbicularis oculi override the superior margin of the eyelid

q: Lecture 6 – Eyelids – slide 30: what does this picture show? Describe it.
a:
Senile ectropion

  • decreasing elasticity of the tissues
  • elongation of the eyelid
  • Tendency to to move off the eyeball
  • treatment
  • blepharoplasty

q: Lecture 6 – Eyelids – slide 35: what does this picture show? Describe it.
a:
Tumors

  • basal cell carcinomas.
  • Etiology:
  • genetic disposition.
  • Increased exposure to the sun’s ultraviolet radiation, carcinogenic substances (arsenic)
  • chronic skin damage
  • arise from the basal cell layers of the epidermis and the sebaceous gland
  • a firm, slightly raised margin with a central crater and superficial vascularization with an increased tendency to bleed
